questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere I normally would not have the opportunity to go to, and I chose the west coast of Canada to experience the nature, especially skiing. I also wanted to go to an english speaking country, as I figured it would be easier to create relations. The ranking of the university was not as important to me as the kind of courses I could take.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They had signs and volunteers to guide you, all you had to do was look confused

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got shown to the place where I could get my student card by one of the volunteers, and another volunteer told me how the canteen worked. You just have to ask the questions and they will help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I could have joined more welcome events than I did, but some of them seemed more directed at first years students rather than exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Towers (dorms) and houses. Most dorms had a mandatory mealplan. I lived in courtyard residence which was newly built and quite nice. Mealplan was mandatory for me, but in hindsight, I would've wanted it anyways.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Not a lot of cooking facilities in the dorms that had mandatory mealplans. I was initially sad about having to be on the mealplan, but it turned out to be the best option in terms of optimizing my time AND it was where i met all the other exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: SFU is on a mountain on its own, so if you live off campus, you miss some of the social factors about being able to meet up all the time. I would spontaneously hang out with whatever friends i met in the dining hall or at the gym, all of which was on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of options

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill out a questionnaire about your living expectations and put the different houses/dorms in a prioritised list. You do not have any advantage being an exchange student, and the deadline to apply is pretty early in the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The website is very thorough.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I initially accidentally signed up for classes in the summer term instead of the fall term, but the team that mails with exchange students helped me a lot even though I exceeded a deadline because of that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even if you apply as an undergraduate, you can still take graduate courses, which you only have to take 3 of to be a full time student. I thought i had to take 4 courses no matter their level because I was enrolled as an undergraduate. Check with KU though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2x 400-level courses and 2x 300-level courses. In hindsight i could've just taken 3x 400-level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They don't really do oral exams. Whenever we had presentations in class, people read out loud from a script almost, which surprised me a lot. They do much more quizzes/assignments during the courses which count a certain percentage of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Radiochemistry (nuclear science)
Materials chemistry
Special topics in analytical chemistry
Cell signalling in development and diseases

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Special topics in analytical chemistry - more discussion based, current tendencies, you choose your own topic for presentation
Cell signalling in development and diseases - really good teacher, very educational

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Medical expenses, but most where covered by insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than i thought, the housing on campus which was just dorms in my case w as mmore expensive than what I pay in copenhagen. Some groceries were super expensive as well but I mostly ate from the meal plan. After the semester had ended we rented an airbnb which was insanely expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of the athletic teams were either closed (you had to be scouted to be there) or they would have try outs, which would be fine if that didn't mean that ideally you should be there for a full year. There were lots of clubs though, and they had a fair where you could walk around and look at the different club stands and ask questions.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: politic, environmental, religious, science related, party, different sports teams.... so many

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: likely a sports team or a hiking club / ski club to have some activities to do while being social.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: HIKE! and ski!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was interesting learning about the indigenous culture, but the culture I was met with everyday was not super different. People in general were a bit more religious than I was used to, but most of my close friends were actually other exchange people, so I was met with so many cultures from europe and australia as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Pretend it's kindergarten and literally just ask people if you can sit down with them and start talking. It was super nerve wrecking at first, but everyone was so keen to get to know new people, so there was very much a vibe of "do you wanna be my friend" and people would just become friends. Also invite people to plans all the time, everyone wants to explore the area anyways - might as well do it together

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some people were very MAGA american, especially noticeable because I was there during the election..

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open heartedness - people would just spark up conversations with strangers which is a very non danish thing to do. And the nature was amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Say yes to every experience

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you show up for all the lectures, you don't have to spend a lot of time on school outside of that, which means you have time for experiences.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends that I have now made all over the world and the things i got to do/see with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I got sick in the very beginning of the stay, which was kind of scary. I wasn't that serious in the end, but navigating a different health care system while not knowing exactly what was wrong and not yet knowing a lot of people that could help me was quite stressful. Everything turned out fine though.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I am sooooo happy that I went on exchange! It seemed like so much work at one point, and I almost considered giving up, but the whole experience has been something I would never want to be without.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
